panel.rangeTitle: Trim characters by event count — drag the low thumb up to hide the barely-developed and focus the busiest arcs.

help.title: Character arc — how to read it

grid.title: The grid
items: Each **row** is a character; **columns** are scenes in reading order.
The **bands** group scenes into chapters (folders) — a character's changes are accumulated per chapter, not per scene, because a trait emerges over a stretch.
A cell's **dots** are the changes in that chapter, colored by kind; click a row to read them all.

rows.● gains: they acquire it (a goal, an ally, leverage)
rows.● revealed: it becomes known — exposed to others or the reader

sheet.title: The Sheet (click a character)
items: The sheet is a **chapter railway**: each chapter is a **station** — a stop (●) where the character changes, a hollow stop (○ ··) for a chapter they're **offstage or static**.
Open a station to read that chapter's **summary**, what they **want**, their **tension** (and with whom), and the **changes** themselves.

provenance.title: Provenance
items: Arc is the analysis agent's reading of the dialogue — its understanding, not authored truth. Re-running analysis refreshes it.

graph.needTwo: Need at least two characters to graph relationships.
